## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Define the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)

## Description

This epic defines the packaging format that makes tutorials versioned and
testable independently of Dashboard releases. A tutorial package carries
metadata describing the tutorial, references the pinned images it runs on, and
includes a validation manifest used to test the tutorial against a target
release. The format is the contract between tutorial content and the Dashboard
tutorial gallery: tutorial authors package against it, and the gallery consumes
packaged tutorials to display and launch them.

## Scope

- Specify the tutorial package metadata (tutorial identity, journey, and the
  information the gallery needs to present and launch the tutorial)
- Specify how a tutorial package references its pinned images
- Specify the validation manifest with which a tutorial is tested against a
  release
- Specify versioning of tutorial packages independent of Dashboard releases
- Provide a reference/sample package demonstrating a conforming tutorial
  package
- The format spans the gallery consumption surface (Dashboard) and the tutorial
  content surfaces (notebook tutorials and pipeline tutorials); it is assigned
  to the Dashboard component as the format's principal consumer

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification covers metadata, pinned images, and the
  validation manifest, and is published where consuming teams can use it.
- A tutorial packaged per the format passes its validation manifest without a
  Dashboard release (demonstrated on the reference package).
- A packaged tutorial carries version information that distinguishes the
  tutorial package version from the Dashboard release.
- The reference package validates successfully and is consumable by the
  tutorial gallery's display and launch path.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): defines the tutorial packaging format so tutorials are versioned
  and testable independently of Dashboard releases.

# Tutorial gallery with one-click launch in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic adds a curated tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a maintained,
tested set of tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch into
their own project with one click. Launching a notebook tutorial opens a
workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook, running the
tutorial's pinned image; launching a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline
into the user's project. The gallery reads tutorial packages that conform to
the tutorial packaging format.

## Scope

- Gallery surface in the Dashboard listing curated tutorials with their
  packaged metadata
- One-click launch of a notebook tutorial: opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook, using the packaged pinned image
- One-click launch of a pipeline tutorial: imports the pipeline into the
  user's project
- Consumption of format-compliant tutorial packages (metadata, pinned images)
  for gallery display and launch
- Tutorial content itself is not authored here — the gallery presents and
  launches packages produced by the tutorial content work streams

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gallery lists tutorials from format-compliant packages with their
  packaged metadata.
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery creates a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook open, running the packaged pinned
  image.
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into the
  user's project.
- End-to-end launch (both modes) is verified against a format-compliant
  tutorial package (a fixture or the first published tutorial).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook,
  or importing the pipeline).

the core getting-started journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training
run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is packaged per the
tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) and

the Dashboard tutorial gallery.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials covering: first workbench, data prep, first
  training run, first deployment, first RAG app
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest)
- Define and run each tutorial's validation manifest against the current
  release
- Keep tutorials maintained as the platform evolves (this release's scope is
  authoring and initial validation against the current release)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the five journeys listed in Scope.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format.
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest against the current release.
- Each tutorial is launchable as a packaged notebook tutorial (opens a
  workbench with the notebook on its pinned image).

  (the notebook-based journeys); each tested against the current release.

# Gallery usage and tutorial contribution documentation

## Description

This epic documents the tutorial gallery for end users and prospective
tutorial contributors: how to browse and launch tutorials from the gallery,
and how to contribute a new tutorial (the tutorial packaging format and its
validation requirements). It follows the Red Hat docs content process and is
authored after the implemented capabilities it describes.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Doc topic: using the tutorial gallery — browsing the curated set and
  launching a tutorial into your project (notebook and pipeline launch modes)
- Doc topic: contributing a new tutorial — the tutorial packaging format
  (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), versioning, and the
  validation requirements a contributed tutorial must pass
- Boundary per strategy out-of-scope: the contribution process is documented,
  but no submission/intake tooling is described as available this release, and
  tutorial content is not localized

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery (browsing and
  both launch modes).
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials,
  including the packaging format and validation requirements.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery,
  the published tutorials, and the packaging format, and accurately reflects
  that submission tooling is not available this release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

Triage: not below-threshold (the strategy explicitly spans three architecturally
distinct work streams with different owners and review processes — Dashboard
product code, curated tutorial content authoring, and documentation — across four
components). Not docs-only (Dashboard code changes are required). Full
decomposition applied.

## Step 1 parse notes

- Affected Components are given as a bare list (Dashboard, Notebooks, Data
  Science Pipelines, Documentation) with no change/owner columns.
- No Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then
  Acceptance Criteria, and no Non-Functional Requirements section — recorded as
  health warnings; teams were derived from the architecture-context owning-team
  fields (see Health Warnings).
- Open Questions: "None" — no unknowns, no conditional ADRs, no pending reviews,
  so no Investigation epics were created.
- No Staff Engineer Input section — the AI-generated technical approach is the
  only guidance; no overrides to log.

## Component graph

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Change | Owner team | Active/Passive |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | Dashboard | New gallery UI + one-click launch mechanics | RHOAI Dashboard | Active |
| Notebooks | Notebooks | Tutorial notebook content authored/tested on workbenches | Workbenches | Active (content) |
| Data Science Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Pipeline tutorial content authored/tested on DSP | RHOAI Pipelines | Active (content) |
| Documentation | Documentation | New doc topics for gallery usage + contribution | RHOAI Documentation (assumed) | Active (docs) |

All four canonical names are verbatim in `.context/rhai-components.txt`.
Non-obvious mapping: the tutorial packaging format epic spans Dashboard,
Notebooks, and Data Science Pipelines (it is the contract between tutorial
content and the gallery); it is assigned the single most-relevant canonical
component **Dashboard** because the gallery is the format's principal consumer
(launch mechanics read the packaged metadata and pinned images). The

3. **Parallel coordination risk** (not a dependency): the gallery (E002) and
